title: Forms of cell-aggregates are shaped chiefly by surface tension toward minimal areas

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Forms of cell-aggregates are shaped chiefly by surface tension toward minimal areas

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The forms of cells in contact with one another, and ultimately of tissues, are determined especially by surface tension, which shows itself in the production of surfaces of (relatively) minimal area.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we shall probably find, and we may at least begin by assuming, that the agency of surface tension is especially manifest and important. The effect of this surface tension will chiefly manifest itself in the production of surfaces _minimae areae_

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Surface tension in cell-aggregates”. Scope: cell-aggregates and tissues of plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cell interfaces and area minimization are quantitatively testable with standard segmentation and physical models. Data are abundant for selected tissues, but causal attribution chiefly to surface tension remains confounded and overly broad.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct cell aggregates, estimate interface areas and tensions, and compare observed tissue geometry with constrained minimal-area predictions and models dominated by adhesion, elasticity, or growth.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Minimal area can emerge from several interacting processes.

The claim's tissue-wide scope exceeds available consistently segmented data.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Segmented tissues already in public archives are enough to test whether cell aggregates approximate surfaces of relatively minimal area. That is the measurable pattern the claim predicts. Naming surface tension as the agency needs a force measurement these datasets do not contain, so the geometric half is testable and the causal half remains confounded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In segmented cell aggregates, compare wall areas and junction angles with the minimal-area surfaces expected for the observed cell volumes. Agreement with minimal-area geometry would support the geometric half; systematic excess area or a different angle rule would refute it, while an independent tension measurement would be required to credit surface tension rather than another minimizing agency.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Minimal-area packing is also predicted by adhesion energy and cortical contractility, which these images do not separate from surface tension.

Plant meristems and a few animal epithelia stand in for tissues in general.
